      About this interactive

      By Elias Rutten · updated November 2026

      The imperial stack is an interactive by Elias Rutten, a political economist and investigative journalist based in Leiden, the Netherlands. It maps how US technology firms, the dollar system and the American state reinforce one another: how platform rents become hardware orders from US allies, how their surpluses return to Wall Street as purchases of US shares rather than reserves, how Washington engineers demand for its own debt, and how the AI build-out is financed, down to the pension savings behind it.

      It is built around Pax Silica, the US-led coalition on AI and semiconductor supply chains. Fourteen scenarios show the stack being switched on or off, among them Starlink over Crimea, Huawei’s fall under US export controls, the Nexperia affair, Russia’s immobilised reserves, Microsoft’s cut-off of Nayara Energy and Tether’s stablecoins in Kenya. Every figure is dated and sourced; “How we count” explains the methods.
